comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C4, C30, C32-C33, C36-C38, C40. Both evaluations find the data convincing that NHR-67 expression determines invasive vs. proliferative fate. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of quantitative imaging and functional perturbations, while peer reviewers describe this as 'convincing data' supporting the primary claims.

Strong agreement on claims C5, C41-C44, C46-C47, C50 regarding HLH-2 regulation of NHR-67. Both find the evidence supported by multiple experimental approaches. OpenEval highlights convergence of gain-of-function and loss-of-function experiments plus yeast one-hybrid data. Peer reviewers accept the regulatory relationship without challenge.

Agreement on claims C6, C51-C57 regarding NHR-67 punctae formation and dynamics. Both evaluations find the time-lapse imaging and fluorescent tagging data convincing. OpenEval emphasizes technical strengths (multiple fluorophores, no fixation artifacts), while peer reviewers describe the observations as 'intriguing' without challenging the data quality.

Agreement on claims C7, C58-C59 regarding liquid-like properties of punctae. Both accept the FRAP data showing recovery kinetics. OpenEval notes modest sample size (n=8) and suggests additional biophysical characterization would strengthen claims, while peer reviewers accept the observations but question functional significance separately.

Agreement on claims C10, C64-C65 regarding colocalization of NHR-67 with Groucho homologs. Both find the quantitative colocalization analysis with Manders' coefficients and appropriate controls convincing. OpenEval emphasizes technical rigor, while peer reviewers note these as 'interesting observations' without disputing measurement quality.

Agreement on claims C60-C62 regarding negative controls for colocalization. Both evaluations accept that the rotation controls and heterozygous positive controls support the interpretation of NHR-67 punctae as distinct subnuclear compartments. Neither challenges these control experiments.

Agreement on claim C72 regarding POP-1 colocalization with NHR-67. Both accept the observation despite lower colocalization coefficients. OpenEval and peer reviewers both acknowledge the technical explanation (strong POP-1 fluorescence outside punctae) without disputing the finding.

Disagreement on claims C66-C67, C91 regarding interpretation of depletion experiments. OpenEval finds the AID-mediated depletion data supported with adequate sample sizes. However, peer reviewers raise significant concerns about whether NHR-67 forms puncta under these conditions, reliance on single markers without lineage analysis, and inability to distinguish misspecification from transdifferentiation. Peer evaluation is UNCERTAIN while OpenEval is SUPPORTED.

Disagreement on claims C78-C82 regarding POP-1 perturbation experiments. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to small sample sizes (n=3), mild knockdown, and low penetrance, but finds the data reasonably supportive. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN but raise different concerns about lineage analysis and whether marker-positive cells arise from AC division versus transdifferentiation. Both acknowledge limitations but from different perspectives.

Partial overlap on claims C74-C76 (OpenEval) and C70-C71, C73-C74, C78-C82 (peer). OpenEval finds reporter assays and literature citations support POP-1 functioning as repressor. Peer reviewers question the broader mechanistic interpretation and cell identity tracking, rating the overall mechanism as UNCERTAIN despite accepting individual observations.

Disagreement on claims C84-C85, C88 regarding NHR-67/UNC-37 interaction. OpenEval finds yeast two-hybrid data with appropriate controls SUPPORTED and consistent with prior predictions. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting the interaction is shown in Y2H but not verified in vivo, and functional significance is not tested. Authors attempted but failed to recover viable CRISPR deletion lines.

Agreement on uncertainty for claims C11, C93, C95-C96 (OpenEval) and C11, C91, C93 (peer) regarding the proposed condensate-mediated repression model. Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the mechanism (sequestration vs. active repression) remains unclear. Peer reviewers emphasize lack of clear link between condensate formation/dissolution and downstream gene activation, stating neither model is fully supported.

Agreement on claim C86 regarding negative Y2H result for NHR-67/POP-1 direct interaction. Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED and consistent with the model where UNC-37 bridges NHR-67 to other repressor components. Neither challenges this negative finding.

Agreement on claim C87 regarding IDR prediction and functional validation. Both evaluations find the computational predictions and Y2H deletion mapping SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the IDR is both necessary and sufficient for UNC-37 binding. Peer reviewers accept the structural analysis without challenge.

Agreement on claim C29 regarding similar Notch signaling in AC and VU cells. Both evaluations find this observation SUPPORTED and useful for ruling out alternative explanations. This helps focus attention on HLH-2 and NHR-67 as key differentially expressed factors.

Partial overlap on claim C73. OpenEval finds the quantitative imaging data showing increased POP-1 in arrested/non-invasive ACs SUPPORTED with adequate sample size. Peer reviewers include this observation within their broader UNCERTAIN evaluation of the POP-1 mechanism, questioning cell identity tracking rather than the measurement itself.

Partial overlap on claims C70-C71. OpenEval finds the quantitative imaging of endogenously tagged POP-1 and colocalization data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers include these observations in their UNCERTAIN evaluation, accepting the data quality but questioning the broader mechanistic interpretation and cell lineage analysis.

Minimal overlap on claim C31. OpenEval finds the literature citations regarding HLH-2 regulation mechanisms SUPPORTED as providing mechanistic context. Peer reviewers accept the HLH-2 regulatory relationship without challenge as part of their broader evaluation of the NHR-67 regulation claims.
